planting.note: Plant only nursery-propagated specimens in spring in wet, acidic, sandy or peaty soil in full sun to partial shade; recreate an open, seepage-bog setting and never collect wild plants.

directions: Chapman's fringed orchid is a striking deep-orange-flowered terrestrial orchid found in a handful of disjunct wet pine savanna and seepage-bog sites across the Gulf Coastal Plain, including deep East Texas populations in the Big Thicket region alongside its presumed parent species. Its fringed lower lip and overall form sit between the showier yellow fringed orchid (Platanthera ciliaris) and the crested yellow orchid (Platanthera cristata), both of which it grows near in the wild, and it typically flowers later in the summer than either. Establish it only from nursery-propagated stock in consistently saturated, acidic, nutrient-poor sandy or peaty soil in full sun, mimicking the open, fire-maintained wet savannas where it naturally occurs; it depends on specific mycorrhizal fungi and resents disturbance once sited. Pair it with pitcher plants, sundews, and other bog specialists in a dedicated wet, sunny bog garden rather than a conventional border.
